Native to mainland Europe, north Africa and Asia, the Argiope bruennichi – commonly known as a wasp spider – is rarely seen in the north and west of Britain. But a fully grown female has been spotted in Cheshire for the first time by conservationists from Chester zoo, who stumbled across the large, brightly… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: España necesita dinero para cuadrar sus cuentas, y Bruselas tiene una amenaza en el horizonte: el IVA al 21% en los bares

A los técnicos de Bruselas no acaba de encajarles que en los restaurantes, cafeterías, bares y hoteles de España se aplique un IVA reducido del 10% (en vez del tipo general del 21%), lo que genera una "gran incidencia presupuestaria" . Los empresarios ya han advertido que una subida del IVA supondría un tiro en el pie tanto del sector como de los hogares… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Noma: The neglected disease devastating children in northern Nigeria
item.description: Noma is a rapidly progressing and often fatal infection of the face and mouth. It mostly affects 2- to 6-year-old children, especially in poor communities. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: Cyanobacterium found in clean lakes shows little toxic potential
item.description: Gloeotrichia echinulata is a type of cyanobacterium that draws scrutiny because it tends to bloom in clear lakes, forming thick mats of visible green or white puffballs in otherwise clean water. Because of the slew of toxic compounds cyanobacteria can produce, blooms (historically called "blue-green algae") are of growing global concern. Yet, a new study by researchers at Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences and Oregon State University suggests this particular species might not deserve its maligned reputation. Fuente: Phys.org.
